sections.heading: C — Driver responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## C — Driver responsibilities (part one)

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
The privilege to drive carries many responsibilities, you and only you are responsible for your actions, and a license holder must know the requirements that keep the privilege of driving in West Virginia [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences, the DMV restricts your license to work, medical, educational and religious purposes until you turn eighteen or present a reinstatement authorization form from the school and pay the reinstatement fee [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
To refer an immediate family member who can no longer drive safely, write a detailed explanation to the DMV Medical Section giving the person's name, address, date of birth and license number if possible, and law enforcement or the person's physician may also submit such information [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
After an unsafe-driver referral the DMV may reexamine the person's driving skills or request updated medical information from the doctor, and may then issue a restricted license or revoke the driving privilege for everyone's safety [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
You may be required to take a medical, written or driving examination when the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified, the result may be suspension, revocation or a restricted license, and refusing the examination is itself grounds for suspension or revocation [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
A crash causing injury or death to any person or property damage over one thousand dollars must be reported by the quickest means, oral or written, within five days to the local police department if it happens inside a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff or the nearest State Police office [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of a crash, your vehicle registration and your driving privilege will be suspended [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Every motorist driving on West Virginia public roads is required by state law to carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance meeting the minimum coverage set by law [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
When you obtain or renew a vehicle registration you must prove West Virginia liability insurance and keep it for the full registration year, and if the insurance is cancelled for any reason you must surrender the registration plate to the DMV [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
A certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance must be carried in the vehicle at all times with a valid registration card, an image on a wireless communication device counts as valid proof, and you must present the proof to an investigating officer after a crash and at any vehicle inspection [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
The DMV may verify insurance at any time during the registration year, including directly and electronically with insurance companies, and failing to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance suspends both the driver's license and the vehicle registration with reinstatement or penalty fees [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
A ticket or crash report showing no West Virginia liability insurance can suspend your license and registration plate, repeat offenses lengthen the license suspension, and reinstatement requires current proof of insurance plus mandatory reinstatement fees [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
Filing false or fraudulent insurance information brings an additional ninety-day license suspension, revocation of the vehicle registration, and possible prosecution carrying a fine of not more than one thousand dollars and jail time of not more than one year [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
Using any electronic communications device while driving on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished with hands-free equipment, and the handbook notes that a driver's concentration drops twenty to thirty-three percent when using a wireless device [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
A hands-free device has a feature that lets the user engage it without either or both hands, and electronic communications devices include cell phones, personal digital assistants, mobile data devices, laptops, pagers, broadband personal communication devices, two-way messaging devices, electronic games and portable computers [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
Using a device that is not hands-free to make a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save or retrieve e-mail, text messages or other electronic data violates the law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
The electronic-device fines are one hundred dollars and zero points for a first offense, two hundred dollars and zero points for a second offense, and three hundred dollars and three points for a third or later offense [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

sections.heading: C — Driver responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## C — Driver responsibilities (part two)

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A03
Using an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the authorities is not a violation, and neither is use by a law-enforcement officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic or authorized emergency vehicle operator performing official duties [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A03
The DMV point system identifies and controls problem drivers by recording every traffic conviction with its date, nature and court, assigning points to in-state and out-of-state moving violations by seriousness, and repeated convictions can build a record that leads to suspension [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
Points remain on your driving record for two years from the conviction date [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
At six or more points the DMV sends a letter of caution urging careful and lawful driving, and at twelve points your driver's license is subject to suspension [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
Completing an approved eight-hour defensive driving class removes three points, but only once every twelve months, only for courses the DMV approves, and not if the class is taken without approval or before the points appear on the record [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
Under the Driver License Compact, traffic violations in other states become part of your West Virginia record with points assessed when warranted, an out-of-state conviction that is grounds for suspension or revocation can suspend or revoke your West Virginia license, and other states may restrict your privilege to drive there [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact a driver may accept a citation for certain violations and continue on, and each member state agrees to suspend its own citizens who fail to comply with the terms of a violation committed in another state [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
Municipal, magistrate and circuit courts must notify the DMV when you fail to appear or fail to comply with any ticket, court order or decision, even a non-traffic matter, and the DMV suspends your license until you prove compliance and pay all penalty fees [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
State law also requires the DMV to suspend your driver's license if you fail to maintain child support payment obligations, so tickets and citations should be handled promptly [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
Giving false information on any license application is illegal, as is using someone else's license, letting another person use yours, letting someone use your identity documents to get a license, or displaying a fictitious license, and the penalty is a ninety-day suspension [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A04
The DMV must revoke a license upon final conviction of manslaughter or negligent homicide from operating a motor vehicle, two or more moving violations as a graduated driver, providing false information to the DMV, or leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A04
Mandatory revocation also follows three reckless driving convictions within twenty-four months, racing on streets or highways, driving while suspended or revoked, and failing to satisfy a civil judgment arising from an automobile crash [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A04
Mandatory revocation further follows a conviction in any state for driving under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances or drugs, a second conviction for failing to pay for gasoline, and any felony committed using a motor vehicle [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A04
Driving while your license is suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason may cause a ninety-day suspension, while driving while revoked for DUI carries a mandatory minimum jail sentence of thirty days to six months and a further six-month revocation of the driving privilege [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A04
All suspension, revocation and reinstatement transactions are handled in person at the Division of Motor Vehicles in Charleston, by mail to its post office box, or online through the DMV self-service site [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A04
The DMV Online Services page lets you check your license status, your total points and your commercial medical certification date, view and buy a driving record for twelve dollars and fifty cents, and pay license reinstatement fees [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A05
Fleeing from an officer carries eight points, the highest value on the point scale [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A05
Six points are assessed for speeding in a school zone, reckless driving, hit and run meaning leaving the scene or failing to reveal identity, and speeding twenty miles per hour or more over the limit [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A05
Speeding fifteen to nineteen miles per hour over the limit carries five points, while speeding eleven to fourteen miles per hour over carries three points [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A05
Three points are assessed for three or more wireless communication device violations, a passing violation, failure to yield, failure to obey a traffic light or a stop sign, hazardous driving, driving left of center, driving too fast for conditions and failure to maintain control of the vehicle [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A05
Three points also apply to careless or hazardous driving, driving the wrong way on a one-way street, littering, an improper lane violation, failure to observe a safety zone, failure to follow a police officer's instructions and driving on the wrong side of the road [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A05
Two points are assessed for following too closely, more than three passengers in the front seat, improper turning, improper backing, an improper signal or no signal, and every other moving violation not listed on the scale [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-wv-class-e:west-virginia-division-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

items.why: Insurance minimums, point values, fines and revocation triggers are recall items served by standard flashcards and quiz questions, so no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook is a periodically revised official edition, so its driver-responsibilities chapter changes at most with a new edition.
